candidates.evidence: Layered selenide with a strong low-frequency mode near 105 cm-1 and several modes between about 150 and 250 cm-1 with no mode above ~250 cm-1, which is qualitatively like the measured pattern. The 205 and 244 cm-1 assignments are recalled from memory, not checked against a reference spectrum.

Layered group-IV monochalcogenide whose Raman modes lie in the 100-260 cm-1 range, consistent with the absence of peaks above ~250 cm-1 here. Recalled literature positions differ from the measured 105/205/244 cm-1 by more than 10 cm-1, so this is a weak match.
Same Pnma layered family as GeS and SnSe, with modes in the 100-250 cm-1 window. No reliable reference positions were available to compare against, so this rests on structural class only.

Layered pentagonal diselenide with several Raman modes between about 130 and 260 cm-1. Recalled positions are approximate and unverified; the pattern here (one weak low-frequency mode and two strong modes near 205 and 244 cm-1) is not confirmed by any reference.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint is null), so there is nothing to check the identification against. The spectrum has three material modes at 104.6, 205.4 and 243.9 cm-1 plus the Si substrate line at 520.6 cm-1, and no other significant features from 60 to 1100 cm-1. Those modes fit a layered, low-symmetry chalcogenide-type structure qualitatively, but three modes without polarization data or a reference library do not identify a specific material. The material is not established; the candidates above are weak, recall-based guesses.

peaks.source: Lorentzian fit over 90-270 cm-1 with polynomial baseline; fit gives 104.62 cm-1, FWHM 8.25 cm-1; full-range fit 104.6 cm-1, FWHM 8.6 cm-1. Mode identity not established.
Lorentzian fit: 205.41 cm-1, FWHM 6.32 cm-1 (fit over 90-270 cm-1); full-range fit 205.4 cm-1. Mode identity not established.
Lorentzian fit: 243.92 cm-1, FWHM 5.15 cm-1 (fit over 90-270 cm-1); full-range fit 243.9 cm-1. Mode identity not established.

Lorentzian fit over 505-537 cm-1 gives 520.62 cm-1 (FWHM 3.54 cm-1). Assignment to the first-order Si Raman mode (about 520.7 cm-1 at room temperature, e.g. Parker, Feldman & Ashkin, Phys. Rev. 155, 712 (1967), recalled and not checked here).

properties.name: phase
properties.source: Three material modes only; no reference library or polarization data available to assign a crystal phase.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Thickness-dependent mode shifts were not measured; no reference frequencies were available to compare against.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: No defect-activated bands (e.g. D-type) seen in the 60-1100 cm-1 range; low-frequency defect signatures cannot be ruled out with this data alone.

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: Mode positions could not be compared with unstrained reference values, so no strain can be inferred.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: No Raman signature of doping was identified; this is not a measurement of doping.

properties.name: substrate_bands
properties.value: Si line only; no SiO2 broad bands (about 440-500 and 800 cm-1) above noise, no significant Si second-order band near 950-1000 cm-1
properties.source: Residual scan after four-peak fit: noise SD about 82 counts; the largest residual bumps (555, 563, 715 cm-1) are about 1.3 sigma of the smoothed residual, which is noise.

citations: Parker, J. H., Feldman, D. W., & Ashkin, M. (1967). Raman scattering by silicon and germanium. Phys. Rev. 155, 712 (recalled, not checked against the source in this session).
limits: The material is not identified. Three material modes (104.6, 205.4, 243.9 cm-1) without a reference spectrum, polarization series, or thickness information cannot single out a compound; the candidates are low-confidence recall-based guesses, and no literature mode table was consulted in this session.

The spectrum was measured at 295 K with 532 nm excitation in backscattering. Peak positions are fitted from a 1.1 cm-1 sampled spectrum, so absolute positions carry a calibration uncertainty of order 0.5 cm-1 (the Si line sits at 520.6 versus a 520.7 reference).

Spectral coverage is 60-1100 cm-1. Modes below 60 cm-1 (e.g. shear or breathing modes) and any modes between 1100 and higher frequencies cannot be seen, so a material with its characteristic modes outside this window would not be identified by this measurement.
Peak assignments to a specific Raman-active irrep or to a specific mode of any candidate could not be made without polarization data; all material peaks are left unassigned.
No cosmic-ray spikes were found: the largest single-point excesses coincide with the broad Si and 205/244 cm-1 peak tops, whose neighbours are also elevated, so they are real peak shape, not spikes.
Among the candidate compounds, the Pnma group (GeS, GeSe) and alpha-In2Se3 are plausible on structural grounds only; this report does not establish any of them.
